notes:
Lead origin: organic inbound from Redwood blog post on doc-search performance. Product: IronQuill builds a search+RAG experience for small law firms (case notes, briefs). They currently use OpenAI embeddings + Pinecone for vectors; experiencing high per-query cost and 700-900ms median response for full RAG flow. Looking at Redwood Hosted API to reduce costs and simplify infra.

Key requirements / quotes:
- Workload: embeddings for ingestion (batch), online query-time retrieval + reranking (top-10 -> cross-encoder scoring), lightweight chat interface later.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 300ms for retrieval+rerank for typical queries, expected peak ~40-75 QPS (mostly bursty during business hours).
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget constraint, "need to keep cost under $0.02 per user query" (customer quote).
- Model preferences: prefer open models for embeddings (cost reasons) and a small cross-encoder for rerank; open to Redwood recommendations/quantized variants.
- Integration questions: how Redwood Hosted API plugs into existing Pinecone index vs using Redwood Optimize + vector-store; can we host embeddings with Redwood and push vectors to Pinecone?
- Security: SOC2 preferred, SSO/SAML for admins, audit logs for data access. No strict residency requirement beyond US.
- Observability: wants per-route token cost breakdown and traceability for rerank decisions.

What we demoed / promised: quickstart keys, sample reranking config (top-k retrieval + cross-encoder rerank), sample cost estimates for hosted embeddings + generation, and notes on batching and prefix caching to reduce per-token cost. SE Liam showed a mock config for 10-item rerank using a small cross-encoder and how Redwood can fallback to a faster ranker when latency spikes.

Concerns called out by customer: "Will switching embeddings break our current semantic similarity?"; worried about tokenization differences causing regressions in legal terms. Also need an internal sign-off on vendor pricing (procurement).

POC ask: customer to provide a 10k-document sample and two canonical query sets (high-frequency legal Qs + long-context briefs). They want a short POC (2 weeks): ingest sample, produce embeddings, run retrieval+rerank, measure p95 latency and answer quality.

Stated next steps: send hosted API pricing + per-call cost math, provide a short rerank config and run an initial demo POC once they upload sample dataset.
